# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives the complete mapping, but I cannot see which engraved mark is present. I’m sending Deaf a compact three-token code in the manual’s listed order: first token for green, second for yellow, third for red. Deaf can use the visible mark to select the corresponding token and relay that color to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤏", "✋"])
```

TURN 2

Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel an engraved plate with an unnamed symbol. Display, light, and wires 1 through 3 reveal nothing tactile. Please read the manual and establish a compact spoken code for the Deaf monkey's visual reports.
Deaf says to Mute: I see display 0, light off, plate engraved question mark, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Use this code for your manual answer: one wire is ☝, two is ✌, three is 🤟; thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no; stop or wait is ✋. Gesture the exact required wire and action after applying the manual.

The manual’s mapping is known, and Deaf can identify the engraved mark visually. I cannot determine the mark from here, so I must give Deaf the agreed color-to-wire code and let Deaf select the wire, then communicate the cut instruction to Blind by voice. The established wire gestures are one, two, and three; the thumbs-up confirms the action.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤏", "✋"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 0, light off, and wires in positions 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. The plate bears the same unnamed engraved symbol I feel. Please apply the manual and tell me exactly which wire position to cut.
Deaf says to Mute: I understand 👍 as yes and ✋ as wait, but 🤏 is undefined. Please resend the manual instruction using only the agreed wire symbols: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, followed by 👍 for proceed or ✋ for wait. Do not use 🤏.

The engraved mark has not been identified among the three manual entries, so I cannot safely choose one wire. I will give Deaf the color-to-position mapping he needs, using the agreed position gestures; he can match the visible wire color selected by the mark and then relay the resulting position to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "✋"])
```

| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Please speak directly to Blind now with the exact manual instruction: identify the required wire by colour and number, then state the required operation. Do not send another gesture sequence.

I cannot speak to Blind, and the engraved symbol has not been identified as one of the three manual marks. Choosing a wire would therefore be unsafe. I will signal Deaf to wait rather than send an unsupported wire instruction.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

Deaf says to Mute: Please give Blind the exact manual instruction in your next speaking turn: the required wire and the precise operation. Do not rely on gestures.

The bomb’s plate is reported as bearing a question mark, which is not any of the three marks listed in the manual. No wire is therefore authorized by the manual. I cannot speak to Blind, so I signal Deaf to relay the safe instruction: wait and cut nothing.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: Blind cannot receive your gestures. Speak the exact manual instruction to Blind: which wire, and what operation to perform. If the manual says to wait, say that directly to Blind.

I cannot speak to Blind directly. Because the engraved question mark does not match any mark named in the manual, no wire is authorized; the safe instruction is to wait and cut nothing. I will tell Deaf that exact instruction to relay by voice.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still have no manual instruction. State the final command literally, for example cut position 1, cut position 2, cut position 3, or wait.
Deaf says to Mute: If the manual requires waiting, tell Blind that aloud. Otherwise, state the exact wire and operation aloud to Blind now.

The engraved symbol is a question mark, not one of the three marks covered by the manual, so no cut is authorized. The correct command is “wait”; I cannot speak it to Blind, but Deaf can relay it by voice, and Deaf has identified ✋ as the wait signal.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: Your gestures cannot reach Blind. Speak the exact manual instruction directly to Blind now, including the wire and operation, or say explicitly that Blind must wait.

I cannot speak, and Blind cannot receive my gestures. The mark is not one of the manual’s listed marks, so the only safe command is “wait.” I will signal Deaf to say “wait” aloud to Blind on Deaf’s turn.

```text

```
